content:
The Factorials & Unit Digits chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Factorials & Unit Digits tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Factorials & Unit Digits

Factorials, trailing zeros in n!, and unit-digit cyclicity of powers.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Trailing zeros in n! = ⌊n/5⌋ + ⌊n/25⌋ + …
  • Unit-digit cycles: 2→(2,4,8,6), 3→(3,9,7,1), 7→(7,9,3,1); length 4.
  • Digits 0,1,5,6 keep their unit digit under any power.
  • For n ≥ 5, n! ends in 0.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Counting only ⌊n/5⌋ and missing higher powers of 5.
  • Using cycle length other than 4 for 2,3,7,8.
  • Forgetting 0,1,5,6 are self-repeating.
